title: AWS managed policy update
description: Lambda added a new AWS managed policy (AWSLambdaNetworkConnectorOperatorPolicy) to grant permissions to create and administer elastic network interface (ENI) resources managed by the Lambda Network Connector. For more information, see Lambda updates to AWS managed policies.

title: AWS managed policy update
description: Lambda updated the AWSLambdaManagedEC2ResourceOperator managed policy to add Amazon CloudWatch permissions (logs:CreateLogGroup, logs:CreateLogStream, logs:PutLogEvents). For details, see Lambda updates to AWS managed policies.

title: AWS managed policy updates
description: Added new API action ec2:DescribeInstanceTypes to AmazonEBSCSIDriverPolicy to enable the EBS CSI Driver to dynamically retrieve volume limit/card information at runtime.

title: Internet Monitor publishes local health events to Amazon EventBridge
description: Internet Monitor now publishes local health events to Amazon EventBridge, in addition to overall (global) health events. Local health events have an impact type of LOCAL_AVAILABILITY or LOCAL_PERFORMANCE.

title: Update to AWS managed policy
description: The AWSSecretsManagerClientReadOnlyAccess managed policy now includes BatchGetSecretValue and ListSecrets permissions. For information, see Secrets Manager updates to AWS managed policies.

title: Amazon MQ now supports configurable storage for RabbitMQ brokers
description:
Amazon MQ now allows you to configure the EBS Disk storage size for RabbitMQ brokers independently of instance type. When creating or updating a broker, you can define a custom storage size, allowing you to right-size storage independently of your instance size to match your specific messaging workload requirements. Configurable storage is available for RabbitMQ M7g brokers on version 4.2 or later using cluster deployments only.

title: AWS Lambda announces self-managed code storage
description:
AWS Lambda now supports self-managed Amazon S3 buckets for code storage, enabling you to reference source code directly from your own S3 buckets without Lambda creating intermediate copies. This eliminates code storage limits and reduces function activation time after function creates and updates by removing the copy step.

title: Introducing Amazon GuardDuty AI Protection for AWS AI workloads
description: Amazon GuardDuty now offers AI Protection, expanding threat detection to AWS AI services including Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker. As organizations rapidly adopt AI, security teams may lack visibility into threats specifically targeting AI workloads, such as anomalous model invocations, cost harvesting attacks, and prompt injection attempts. title: AWS Security Hub now provides AI inventory for organization-wide visibility of AI assets
description: Today, AWS announces that AWS Security Hub now provides an AI inventory, giving central security teams a continuously updated, organization-wide view of AI assets and their security posture. As organizations rapidly deploy AI agents, models, and pipelines, security teams may lack visibility into what AI assets exist across their organization. Without centralized visibility connecting AI assets to active threats and misconfigurations, organizations cannot secure what they don't know exists.

title: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna now generally available on Amazon Bedrock
description: GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna are now generally available on Amazon Bedrock, bringing the smartest family of models from OpenAI yet to Bedrock's next-generation inference engine built for high-performance, security and reliability. GPT-5.6 sets a new standard for intelligence and efficiency, allowing you to solve harder problems in less time and with more intelligence per token. title: Amazon Timestream for InfluxDB now publishes database state change events to Amazon EventBridge
description:
Amazon Timestream for InfluxDB now publishes events to Amazon EventBridge when your database instances or clusters undergo state changes. Events are emitted for lifecycle operations including creation, deletion, compute and storage scaling, parameter group updates, maintenance windows, and reboot — covering both successful completions and failures.

title: AWS Config now supports 191 additional managed rules
description: AWS Config now supports 191 additional managed rules across key services including Amazon Bedrock, Amazon SageMaker, Amazon ECS, Amazon EKS, Amazon RDS, Amazon Redshift, Amazon S3, and Amazon CloudTrail. This expansion increases built-in governance coverage across AI workloads and core cloud infrastructure. Examples of the new managed rules include evaluating resource configurations for encryption, logging, public access, network security, data protection, and other operational best practices

title: AWS Security Hub extends unified security management to Microsoft Azure
